subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime create and patch operations fail closed on all legacy ownerless session rows, with one shared authorization contract coordinated across this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103534?
rationale: The safe default prevents unprovable plugin adoption, but it deliberately breaks any existing plugin workflow that consumes ownerless rows; neither automation nor test results can choose that compatibility and security policy.

options.title: Approve fail-closed and unify
options.body: Use one shared helper and authoritative-row recheck across create, delete, and patch, reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes, and document the operator/non-plugin recovery path.

options.title: Define a migration first
options.body: Pause both PRs until a safe, explicit migration can identify ownership for legacy rows without permitting arbitrary plugin adoption.

options.title: Preserve legacy access
options.body: Keep ownerless rows accessible to plugin runtimes, accepting that exact plugin ownership cannot be enforced for those persisted sessions.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed and unify
recommendation.body: Use one shared helper and authoritative-row recheck across create, delete, and patch, reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes, and document the operator/non-plugin recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and contributor discussion already identified this person for the ownerless-session security and compatibility decision.
